title: Short Stuff: Body Under The Bed
summary: Short Stuff episode on the urban legend of finding a dead body under a hotel bed or mattress. Josh and Chuck cover Snopes' findings that such cases are real and have happened many times, including a 2003 Kansas City motel case where a guest stayed three nights before housekeeping found a decomposing body, a Pasadena case, and German tourists' complaints in Florida and Atlantic City. They note Snopes traced around ten cases between 2002 and 2010. The hosts then discuss how bodies end up in hotel rooms, mostly murders where a body is hidden, and also hotel suicides, with Las Vegas and casinos cited for high suicide rates. They mention a hotel-management article on responding to guest deaths (including keeping a large tarp for atrium leaps), crime scene cleanup companies whose business is largely hotel suicide cleanups, hotels gutting rooms after deaths, and a Reddit thread of front-desk worker stories.
topics: Reddit tales from the front desk

segments.title: Hotel body under the bed urban legend
segments.summary: Josh introduces the urban legend of a dead body hidden under a hotel bed, mentioning a similar Eddie Murphy elevator tale as a comparison. He says Snopes confirmed the legend is true and that such cases have occurred many times.

segments.title: Documented hotel body cases
segments.summary: The hosts walk through specific cases: a 2003 Capri Motel case in Kansas City where a guest stayed three nights before a body was found under the bed; a case at the Burgundy Motor Inn in Atlantic City where German tourists complained; two German-tourist cases in Florida; and a Pasadena Travel Lodge case where a woman was found under a mattress ten days after complaints. Snopes found about ten such cases between 2002 and 2010, and the hosts note cases continue.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Hosts take a break before returning to the topic.

segments.title: How bodies end up in hotel rooms
segments.summary: Hosts discuss how bodies get into hotel rooms, saying the cases are typically murders where a body is hidden, and note the horror of both the unknowing guest and the indignity of the body being stashed.

segments.title: Hotel suicides, Las Vegas, and cleanup
segments.summary: The hosts turn to suicides in hotels, which are often chosen to spare family or avoid media attention. Casinos and Las Vegas are cited for high suicide rates. A hotel-management article suggests keeping a large tarp for atrium leaps. A San Francisco crime scene cleanup company says hotel suicide cleanups are most of its business, and hotels often gut rooms afterward. A Reddit thread of front-desk stories is mentioned, and the hosts note such deaths often happen in the nicest rooms.
topics: Reddit tales from the front desk

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh close the episode and the show's sign-off plays.
